correctness.rationale: For each m<=N the rank inequality is equivalent to vanishing on all inverse pairs because C=N works off the zero locus; direct-sum padding reduces to m=N. Rational canonical form proves the universal annihilator P_{q,N}, both inclusions via companion blocks of maximum feasible exponent. The two-sided inverse quotient is exactly k[t,t^-1], the P degrees grow unboundedly, and equal-rank XY-I/YX-I establishes the global equality class. Every degree-L free polynomial maps to Laurent support [-L,L], forcing 2L>=D; the symmetrically shifted P provides equality. The verifier reconstructs P and checks GF(2), GF(3) exhaustive small cases including 6839 full matrix pairs. General case uses proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: The motivating October 2026 paper proves homogeneous rank domination and shows a single nonhomogeneous inverse-pair counterexample over characteristic zero. Inspected subsequent rank-equivalence, earlier rationally-resolvable ideal results and a sparsity comparison do not supply the finite-field complete truncated ideal or sharp first false-positive degree. Actual semantic database searches yielded no stronger match. The known rational canonical form factors are acknowledged as classical. An unidentified equivalent older finite-general-linear-group polynomial-identity treatment remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Finite matrix tests for nonhomogeneous rank inequalities are susceptible to false positives. The result supplies the complete finite-size rank-domination ideal for a canonical obstruction, the optimal degree at which finite testing first fails, and a universal necessary-and-sufficient degree/size verification boundary for all candidate free polynomials. It is an infinite, naturally motivated q,N classification, not a small isolated computation or a routine check; the binary degree-two witness exhibits the first genuinely nontrivial barrier.
